chunks: O my people, authority is yours today being the most powerful in the land; but who will save us from the scourge of God if it fall upon us?" "I show you," said the Pharaoh, "only what I see (is right), and guide you but to the right path."
ai.seo_question: What did Pharaoh say about his people's authority and his own guidance?
ai.summary: In Surah Ghafir, Pharaoh’s declaration highlights the paradox of temporal power amidst impending divine retribution, a theme central to Shia exegesis regarding the arrogance of tyrants who mistake political dominance for spiritual security. His claim of guiding his people to 'the right path' (sabil al-rashad) is often interpreted as self-deception, contrasting with the true guidance of the Imams. This passage underscores the Shia theological concept that worldly authority without divine alignment is ultimately futile.
